findings.description: `merge_of_target` reads the whole worktree MERGE_HEAD file with `cat` before checking its length. A session can make that file a huge sparse file, or a symlink to one. Every later Bash pre and post check then runs past the 5-second hook timeout and fails open, even for sessions that are not merging.
findings.body:
**An unbounded read of MERGE_HEAD lets a session switch off the Bash re-check**

`merge_of_target` runs first in every `out_of_scope` call (`MERGED=$(merge_of_target) || MERGED=`, line 499). That call comes before the `git status` and before the 200-record cap, so it runs on every Bash PreToolUse and PostToolUse, whether or not a merge is in progress. It does this:

```sh
  [ -f "$HEAD_FILE" ] || return 1
  MERGING=$(cat -- "$HEAD_FILE") || return 1
  case "$MERGING" in *[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
```

- `HEAD_FILE` is `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/worktrees/<id>/MERGE_HEAD`. It is outside the worktree, so `git status` never reports a write to it. Decision 99 already notes that a session can write its own MERGE_HEAD.
- `[ -f ]` follows symlinks, and `cat` reads the whole file before the hex and length checks run.
- One `truncate -s 1T "$(git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"` therefore runs every later check past `HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5`. The hook then fails open, so out-of-scope Bash writes are no longer recorded or refused. This is the same "every later check hung too" pattern decision 63 closed for the fifo.
- Decision 99's ceilings accept forged index entries that hide one path. They do not accept a re-check that times out on every call.

This PR adds the read. No earlier hook read an unbounded file under `.git`.

**Fix:** bound the read. With 66 bytes, a 64-hex id plus its newline fits, and any 67th byte stays in the value, so the `case` check rejects it as `cat` did. Separately, the `cat-file -e "$MERGING^{commit}"` line is redundant: `TIP` is already resolved with `^{commit}`, and the equality test that follows it implies a commit. Dropping that line also removes the chance of a promisor lazy fetch on an object id the session chose.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/79d087c66cc2da6be3d1cfd468d83f4abdab118c/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L328-L337

findings.description: The Edit conflict exemption checks only the shape of `old_string`, never where it sits in the file. An `old_string` can open partway through a line ending in `<<<<<<<`, or stop at `>>>>>>>` before the rest of the label (or the `\r` on a CRLF file). That leaves label text or a stray `\r` in the out-of-scope file, contrary to the comment's "from its <<<<<<< line to its >>>>>>> line". The gate's scope audit still refuses the result, so this is not a bypass. Requiring a line boundary on both sides of the match in the file would close it.

During a merge, the Bash re-check skips a path that matches the tip in the worktree (`git diff <tip>`), even if different content is staged. So `printf evil > X && git add X && git show <tip>:X > X` leaves the bad content staged and unflagged until commit. Adding a `--cached "$MERGED"` listing to `differs` would close it.

The Edit hook comment (and the matching sentence in decision 99) says a hand-staged conflict "earns nothing". But `git update-index --index-info` can stage exactly `HEAD:<path>` and `<tip>:<path>` at stages 2 and 3 without a merge, which decision 99's own ceiling admits. The comment should say the gate's scope audit is what refuses this case.

A live peer whose branch already contains `mergeCommit` is still steered to take main in, and is told to commit its work and run a rebase that does nothing. This happens, for example, when two PRs land one after the other and the first fast-forward brings in both. Skipping peers where `isAncestor(repoPath, mergeCommit, refs/heads/<branch>)` holds would avoid it.

`gitDiffPaths` uses git's default rename detection, so a file the landed PR renamed is listed only under its new name. A peer editing the old path, a classic rename/modify conflict, gets no steer. The generated hooks pass `--no-renames` for this reason; the landed-files listing could do the same.

A `main-landed` steer is recorded as a `steer` event, which `openQuestion` (dashboard.service.ts) treats as the answer to an open `pup session ask` question. So a land can silently clear a peer's question from the needs-you list. Decision 99 accepts this only for `peer-joined` steers: either document it for `main-landed` too or have the inbox ignore this kind.

`safe_git` renders `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` with hand-rolled `'${arg}'` quoting, which does not escape `'`, while the same file now imports `shellWord`. Using `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG.map(shellWord).join(' ')` keeps one quoting path, and a future pin containing a quote cannot break the generated hook.

`shellWord` is now exported while `merge-gate.service.ts:624` keeps a private `shellWord` that always quotes. Two same-named helpers in core now quote the same target ref differently: `mainLandedMessage` and the gate's fresh-base message both build `git rebase refs/heads/<target>`. Have merge-gate import the exported one, or share one target-ref helper.

The new merge-of-target suite copies `GIT_ENV`, the bash pre/command/post driver, `violations()` and the hook runner from the decision-63 re-check suite. The copies have already drifted: the runner drops the UTF-8 locale, and the `GIT_ENV` copy drops its comment. Lifting them to file scope would share them.

Two Edit-exemption rules have no test. One is the "empty side only with its final newline" branch: the fixture block has no empty side, so `''` is refused either way. The other is the diff3 `|||||||` base-marker branch.

The `steerOverlappingSessions` JSDoc restates most of decision 99's steer paragraph, including the failure list and a "not reported yet" tail that will go stale. general.md asks JSDoc to carry only the why: keep the invariants (it runs after `landed`, it is best effort, only an interrupt stops it) and cite decision 99 for the rest.

The call-site comment's "why merge, not rebase" half restates `mainLandedMessage`'s JSDoc, which the seam-duplication rule (general.md, AGENTS.md §Comments) forbids. Trim it to the part that is new here: a `prUrl` on the newest merge event means an open PR.

The ~10-line comment above `RESOLUTION` copies decision 99's conflict-exemption rules almost word for word. Keep the 3–4 non-obvious WHYs (a CR-ended marker is still a marker, the empty side takes the final newline, the stage check) and point to decision 99 for the rest.

In decision 99, "a steer failure past a refused paste or a stop is not rethrown" reads as if a refused paste or a stop is rethrown. That contradicts the earlier sentence and the code, which swallow every non-interrupt failure. Suggested wording: "a refused paste or a stop is not rethrown here either".
In decision 99's "Tests:" paragraph, one line runs far past the file's wrap and the next breaks mid-sentence ("…shell-quotes a target holding `;`. In a real repo with a"). Reflow it.

The hooks' `git status`, and now `git diff <tip>`, can run a clean filter the session armed through `.git/info/attributes`, which has no `-c` disarm. Such a filter can hide a write or hang the hook past its timeout. pup's own calls pair `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` with the `armedGitDrivers` refusal (decision 50); the hooks have no equivalent.

A commit-graph planted in the shared objects directory can give the target tip a different tree, the same swap the new `core.useReplaceRefs=false` pin closes. Disabling replace refs also lets git load the graph. Consider adding `-c core.commitGraph=false` to `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` and a line in decision 99.

The new land-time `git diff` over each live peer branch runs without `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` and the transport pins, so a planted promisor remote could run a session-named transport as the operator. The overlap radar and the gate run the same unpinned diff, and decision 99 already lists these pins as owed.
